title: Coordinate projections
statement:
Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian affine scheme with function field $k(S)$,
and let $Y\to S$ be projective. Choose a finite affine open cover
$Y=\bigcup_\alpha Y_\alpha$ and closed immersions
$Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$ with $m_\alpha\geq1$, and write
$t_{\alpha r}:Y_\alpha\to\mathbf A^1_S$ ($1\le r\le m_\alpha$) for the
coordinate functions.

1. If $X\subset Y$ is open and $\dim X_{k(S)}\leq n$, then for every
   $\alpha,r$ the generic fibre of $t_{\alpha r}:X\cap Y_\alpha\to\mathbf A^1_S$
   has dimension at most $n-1$.
2. Suppose given a dense open $V_{\alpha r}\subset\mathbf A^1_S$ for each
   $\alpha,r$, and let

   $$
   G=\bigcup_{\alpha,r}t_{\alpha r}^{-1}(V_{\alpha r})\subset Y.
   $$

   After shrinking $S$, the reduced closed complement $Z=Y\setminus G$ is
   finite over $S$.

proof.text:
(1) The dimension of an integral scheme of finite type over a field is the
transcendence degree of its function field. Consider an irreducible component
of $X_{k(S)}\cap Y_\alpha$ with function field $L$. If $t_{\alpha r}$ is
algebraic over $k(S)$ on it, the component does not dominate
$\mathbf A^1_{k(S)}$ and does not meet the generic fibre of $t_{\alpha r}$.
Otherwise $t_{\alpha r}$ is transcendental and

$$
\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(S)(t_{\alpha r})}L=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(S)} L-1\leq n-1.
$$

(2) Let $t$ be the coordinate of $\mathbf A^1_S$. The ideal of the closed
complement of $V_{\alpha r}$ contains a nonzero polynomial
$P_{\alpha r}\in\mathcal O(S)[t]$. After inverting the leading coefficients of
these finitely many polynomials we may assume that all of them are monic. The
function $P_{\alpha r}(t_{\alpha r})$ vanishes at every point of the reduced
affine scheme $Z\cap Y_\alpha$, hence is zero in its coordinate ring. That ring
is therefore a quotient of

$$
\mathcal O(S)[t_{\alpha1},\ldots,t_{\alpha m_\alpha}]/
      (P_{\alpha1}(t_{\alpha1}),\ldots,P_{\alpha m_\alpha}(t_{\alpha m_\alpha})),
\qquad\text{(G20)}
$$

which is generated as an $\mathcal O(S)$-module by the monomials whose exponent
in each variable is less than the degree of the corresponding polynomial. Thus
each $Z\cap Y_\alpha$ is finite over $S$, and $Z\to S$ has finite fibres. To
conclude that $Z\to S$ is finite we use that $Z$ is closed in the projective
$Y$: then $Z\to S$ is proper with finite fibres, hence finite (Stacks, Tag
[02LS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02LS)).
